findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh stage-layouts apt-get install line and expect_output_has "today's libraries pass the written floor" "highest=GLIBC_2.38"
findings.obligation: Obligation (a): today build passes the floor and the highest GLIBC version is parsed; design expects highest=GLIBC_2.38
findings.observation: The WebKit package is installed unpinned (libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0) from a moving archive; the image digest pins the base only. An exact GLIBC_2.38 pin turns an archive update that still satisfies the floor into a false red, not a silent pass. Medium.
findings.remediation: Pin the package version in stage-layouts, or derive the expected highest independently by running readelf -V in the oracle and compare; keep requiring a non-empty parsed highest version.

findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-glibc-floor.sh lines 354-365 (line_number_of check-glibc-floor.sh on the workflow file)
findings.obligation: Promise P2 and Expectation E4: CI fails a build whose AppImage needs a newer glibc than the floor, so it is never released
findings.observation: The check is a static order of first-occurrence line numbers. A comment naming check-glibc-floor.sh satisfies it. The oracle does not require a run: step, does not reject continue-on-error, and does not require the extracted squashfs-root argument, so a floor step that cannot fail the job passes. Medium.
findings.remediation: Parse the workflow YAML (actionlint is available) and assert that the step between the libssl step and the upload step has a run invoking check-glibc-floor.sh on the extracted directory, with no continue-on-error. Keep the order check on step indexes, not first-occurrence lines.
